title: feat: depth output for the Gaussian splatting backends
abstract:
Native render passes and either Gaussian backend share per-path `D32_SFLOAT` attachments through `DepthAttachment`. `DepthState` independently controls testing and writing, while `outputDepth` separately controls Gaussian depth-buffer export. Both backends provide accumulated-opacity and nearest-opaque-splat estimates with configurable opacity thresholds.

Native passes use pipeline depth state. Compute splatting reads and updates GPU snapshots; raster splatting uses read-only native tests, fragment atomics for nearest-splat depth, and a depth-only compute pipeline for accumulated opacity or devices without fragment atomics. Raster color and computed depth share center visibility so culled edge splats do not write invisible surfaces.

Tests cover rendering order, independent controls, clearing and preservation, separate paths, rejected extents/path counts, selectable estimates and raster depth visibility. The guide and requirements describe the available API, implementation costs and translucent-surface limitations.

Validation: Windows Debug shaders, engine and tests rebuilt; 63 Gaussian/render-target/depth-composition tests passed with Vulkan validation enabled; Sphinx HTML with warnings treated as errors; clang-format 23.1.2, header guards and example-doc checks. The final stacked tree was verified identical to the reviewed pre-split checkpoint.

Part 4 of 4. Review and merge in this order:

1. #69 — directory organization and existing-behavior documentation → `develop`
2. #70 — cropped-view, image-layout and shader-build fixes → #69
3. #71 — Gaussian depth export → #70
4. This PR — shared depth composition and selectable estimates → #71

Each PR contains one thematic commit and targets the previous branch so its diff contains only its own changes. Retarget the next PR to `develop` after merging its predecessor. Downstream #47, #48 and #68 are intentionally left for a rebase after this stack is merged.
